entry.title: Teen spending up 6% as they trade athletic apparel for fashion
entry.summary: While footwear was down and traditional athletic brands lost share, Target and brands including On gained ground, per a survey from Piper Sandler.

entry.title: Target unwraps high-concept holiday ads focused on gift-giving academy
entry.summary: Actor D’Arcy Carden serves as Chief Giftologist in a new campaign that will be supported by a bigger creator push around YouTube and TikTok.

entry.title: Adidas’ record Q3 is salt in the wound for Nike
entry.summary: Preliminary figures show revenue reaching $8.1 billion, as the sportswear giant takes “significant” share from its rival.

entry.title: Amazon eyes 300K holiday hires
entry.summary: The e-commerce giant is increasing U.S. holiday staffing by 20% compared to the past three seasons.

entry.title: Why customers are fed up with AI chatbots
entry.summary: Few things will cause a customer to immediately request — or demand — a live agent like a bot that misunderstands them.

entry.title: Tractor Supply taps former Home Depot exec as chief digital, technology officer
entry.summary: Fahim Siddiqui will oversee digital operations and work to bolster long-term growth by improving the retailer’s customer experience.

entry.title: EBay cuts 1K jobs, downsizing for the second time this year
entry.summary: The layoffs, affecting about 9% of the marketplace giant’s global workforce, will impact all regions where it operates.

entry.title: Walmart welcomes external AI agents — with some guardrails
entry.summary: The mass retailer is focused on transparency and customer control with a new AI agent profile feature and updated agent terms.

entry.title: David’s Bridal to spin off Pearl into stand-alone, publicly traded company
entry.summary: David’s Bridal CEO Kelly Cook is expected to become the chief executive of Pearl, which will own the wedding retailer’s intellectual property and brand.

entry.title: Beyond Yoga aims to have ‘many’ stores. They’ll probably be yellow.
entry.summary: CEO Nancy Green says the brand color is reflective of a broader focus on joy — and making progress over perfection.
